name: Service Level Objective / Reliability Commitment
purpose: Represent immutable SLI and SLO policy versions, windowed evaluations, error-budget rules and observability bindings without owning metric formulas, telemetry observations, service identity or contractual SLA obligations.

owns: SLI specification bound to one metric-definition version
immutable SLO policy versions and subject placement
window definitions eligibility exclusions and coverage thresholds
append-only SLO evaluations and restatement lineage
error-budget policy and explicit transition rules
effective-dated observability bindings and evaluation provenance
delegates: metric formula population unit dimensions and null semantics to Metric Definition
raw observations absence and censoring to WM-MAT-008
service identity and expected outcome to WM-ACT-004
contractual obligations obligees credits remedies and enforceability to WM-ECO-006
calendar identity timezone and period conventions to WM-XCT-009
composite User Journey identity to an identifier-unassigned candidate
excludes: copied live metric values on the policy
success verdict inferred from missing data

relations.purpose: Resolve immutable observations, absence reasons, time and provenance.
Attach the reliability commitment to a service without importing service identity.
Allow a contractual agreement to cite policy and evidence while obligations and remedies remain contract-owned.
Pin calendar identity, timezone and period conventions for aligned windows.

operations.effect: Issue an immutable SLI specification bound to one metric definition.
Issue an immutable policy version with target window coverage and budget rules.
Create an effective-dated source and collection binding.
Append a window evaluation with counts coverage evidence and verdict.
Append a corrected evaluation while preserving the predecessor.
Issue a successor policy and explicit budget transition for a changed window definition.

invariants: Every SLO policy version names one immutable SLI version, target and window definition.
Metric formula population unit dimensions and null semantics are referenced rather than restated.
Raw observations remain externally mastered and are never copied into the SLO policy.
No data, no eligible traffic, indeterminate and met are distinct outcomes.
Missing telemetry never counts as a good event.
Coverage below the declared threshold yields unknown-insufficient-coverage.
Every evaluation records evaluator identity and version plus offset-qualified window bounds.
Material change to formula predicates eligibility exclusions target window or coverage mints a successor policy version.
Error budget never silently crosses a window-definition change.
Exclusions are prior authorized capped counted and reported.
Retroactive exclusion creates a linked restatement and never erases observations or denominator history.
Component or instance indicators are diagnostic unless a declared aggregation rule connects them to the commitment.
SLO policy and contractual SLA obligation have different authority bases and lifecycles.
Superseded policies bindings and restated evaluations remain historically resolvable.
Access to an evaluation cannot exceed access to its observation evidence.
